title: The Orchard of Port Mahon
premise: In the winter of 1917, Ulyana Yarrow arrives at the garrison hospital of Port Mahon, a river town whose only link to the world is a seasonal bridge. As a nurse, she keeps a private ledger recording the names and small histories of wounded soldiers that official reports erase, believing that history belongs to other people, elsewhere. When the bridge closes for the season, she is trapped among the very people she documented, including Major Aldous Crane, an officer determined to confiscate her ledger to protect reputations, and Tomas, a wounded cartographer who helps her see her record as something that must survive. As ice cracks on the river and the workshop where she copies and hides the ledger faces demolition on Crane's orders, Ulyana races to finish the true account before the thaw brings both rescue and erasure; in the end she entrusts the finished ledger to the townspeople who smuggle it across the breaking ice, choosing at last to sign her own name to history.
about_author: Emrys Vane is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing unclaimed letters from forgotten wars. The Orchard of Port Mahon is their second novel, written in a converted cider house on the Welsh border.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Names
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She arrives at Port Mahon as the bridge closes, settling into the hospital's rhythms and beginning her secret ledger of names the officers omit. A quiet chapter establishing her belief that history happens elsewhere, and her careful invisibility. Emotional beat: guarded tenderness — she records others' lives precisely so she need not live her own.

chapters.title: What the Ice Keeps
chapters.summary: Alternating Ulyana and Tomas POV. Trapped by winter, Ulyana grows close to Tomas, a wounded cartographer who maps the town from memory, while Major Crane begins noticing missing names in official reports. The workshop becomes their refuge. Emotional beat: belonging arrives uninvited — Ulyana realizes the ledger has made her part of the story she documents.

chapters.title: The Order of Erasure
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV with interludes from Crane. Crane orders the workshop demolished and demands the ledger, exposing how power rewrites memory to protect itself. Ulyana hides pages in the orchard while the hospital fractures into loyalty and fear. Climax: a midnight confrontation in the workshop as axes arrive, and Ulyana refuses to surrender the names. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into defiance.

chapters.title: Before the River Breaks
chapters.summary: Ulyana and communal town POV. With the ice cracking, the townspeople smuggle the finished ledger across the river in pieces hidden in seed crates, each carrier memorizing a page in case the paper is lost. Crane, facing his own omission in the record, lets them pass. Resolution: Ulyana signs her name beneath the last entry. Emotional beat: release — invisible no longer, she belongs to the history she saved.
